en: Saṁyutta Nikāya 30.1 (SN 30.1, PTS SN iii 246) 1. Supaṇṇavagga Suddhikasutta (The Simple Discourse) At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, there are these five aggregates subject to clinging. What five? The form aggregate subject to clinging, the feeling aggregate subject to clinging, the perception aggregate subject to clinging, the volitional formations aggregate subject to clinging, and the consciousness aggregate subject to clinging. These, bhikkhus, are the five aggregates subject to clinging.”
The setting was at Sāvatthī.
“Monks, there are these four origins of supaṇṇas.
Which four?”
“Bhikkhus, there are these four modes of birth for supaṇṇas: egg-born supaṇṇas, womb-born supaṇṇas, moisture-born supaṇṇas, and spontaneously born supaṇṇas.
These, bhikkhus, are the four modes of birth for supaṇṇas. Thus was the first [sutta].

Saṁyutta Nikāya 30.2 (SN 30.2, PTS SN iii 246) 1. Supaṇṇavagga Harantisutta “Monks, there are these four kinds of supaṇṇas who carry off beings. What four? The supaṇṇa who carries off beings by means of his strength; the supaṇṇa who carries off beings by means of his power; the supaṇṇa who carries off beings by means of his magical power; and the supaṇṇa who carries off beings by means of his supernormal power. These, monks, are the four kinds of supaṇṇas who carry off beings. In the same way, monks, there are these four kinds of persons who carry off beings. What four? The person who carries off beings by means of his strength; the person who carries off beings by means of his power; the person who carries off beings by means of his magical power; and the person who carries off beings by means of his supernormal power. And how, monks, does a person carry off beings by means of his strength? Here, monks, a certain person is himself virtuous, yet he encourages others in the non-arising of unarisen evil, unwholesome qualities; he encourages others in the abandoning of arisen evil, unwholesome qualities; he encourages others in the arising of unarisen wholesome qualities; and he encourages others in the maintenance, non-decline, increase, expansion, and fulfillment by development of arisen wholesome qualities. This, monks, is called a person who carries off beings by means of his strength. And how, monks, does a person carry off beings by means of his power? Here, monks, a certain person is himself powerful, yet he encourages others in the non-arising of unarisen evil, unwholesome qualities... [as above] ...he encourages others in the maintenance, non-decline, increase, expansion, and fulfillment by development of arisen wholesome qualities. This, monks, is called a person who carries off beings by means of his power. And how, monks, does a person carry off beings by means of his magical power? Here, monks, a certain person is himself possessed of magical power, yet he encourages others in the non-arising of unarisen evil, unwholesome qualities... [as above] ...he encourages others in the maintenance, non-decline, increase, expansion, and fulfillment by development of arisen wholesome qualities. This, monks, is called a person who carries off beings by means of his magical power. And how, monks, does a person carry off beings by means of his supernormal power? Here, monks, a certain person is himself accomplished in direct knowledge, yet he encourages others in the non-arising of unarisen evil, unwholesome qualities... [as above] ...he encourages others in the maintenance, non-decline, increase, expansion, and fulfillment by development of arisen wholesome qualities. This, monks, is called a person who carries off beings by means of his supernormal power. These, monks, are the four kinds of persons who carry off beings.”
The setting was at Sāvatthī.
"Bhikkhus, there are these four origins of supaṇṇas.
Which four?"
“Egg-born...
[as before] ...These, monks, are the four modes of birth for *supaṇṇas*.
Among them, monks, egg-born *supaṇṇas* carry off only egg-born *nāgas*, not those born from a womb, nor those born from moisture, nor those of spontaneous birth.”
In this regard, monks, the egg-born supaṇṇas carry off nāgas that are egg-born and womb-born, but not those that are moisture-born or spontaneously born.
In this regard, monks, the moisture-born supaṇṇas carry off nāgas that are egg-born, womb-born, and moisture-born, but not those that are spontaneously born.
In this regard, monks, the spontaneously born supaṇṇas carry off nāgas that are egg-born, womb-born, moisture-born, and spontaneously born.
“Monks, these are the four wombs of the supaṇṇas.
The second.
*Saṃyutta Nikāya* 30.3. (SN 30.3, PTS SN iii 247)
1. Supaṇṇavagga.
Dvayakārīsutta.
The Setting is at Sāvatthī.
A certain bhikkhu approached the Blessed One; having approached and paid homage to the Blessed One, he sat down to one side. As he was sitting there, that bhikkhu said this to the Blessed One:
“What, venerable sir, is the cause, what is the reason, why someone here, with the breakup of the body, after death, is reborn in the company of egg-born supaṇṇas?
“Here, bhikkhu, someone acts in two ways by way of body, acts in two ways by way of speech, and acts in two ways by way of mind.”
He has heard:
“The egg-born supaṇṇas are long-lived, beautiful, and abound in happiness.
It occurs to him:
‘Oh, that after the breakup of the body, following death, I might be reborn in the company of the egg-born supaṇṇas!
He, with the breakup of the body, after death, is reborn in the company of the egg-born supaṇṇas.
This, monk, is the cause, this is the condition, by which someone here, with the breakup of the body, after death, is reborn in the company of the egg-born supaṇṇas.”
Third.
Saṃyutta Nikāya 30.4–6 (SN 30.4, PTS SN iii 247) 1.
Supaṇṇavagga (The Chapter on Supaṇṇas)
The Triplet on the Discourse Concerning One Who Does Two [Wrongful Acts], etc., Second.
The setting was at Sāvatthī.
Seated to one side, that bhikkhu said this to the Blessed One:
“Venerable sir, what is the cause, what is the reason, why someone here, with the breakup of the body, after death,
is reborn in the company of the fire-born supaṇṇas … the moisture-born supaṇṇas … or the spontaneously born supaṇṇas?”
“Here, bhikkhu, a certain person acts dualistically by way of body, acts dualistically by way of speech, and acts dualistically by way of mind.
He has heard:
‘The supaṇṇas who are born spontaneously have long lives, are beautiful, and abound in happiness.’”
It occurs to him:
"O, that after the breakup of the body, after death, I might be reborn in the company of the spontaneously born supaṇṇas!
After the breakup of the body, after death, he is reborn in the company of the spontaneously born supaṇṇas.
“This, bhikkhu, is the cause, this is the condition, by which someone here, with the breakup of the body, after death, is reborn in the company of spontaneously born *supaṇṇas*.
The sixth.
*Saṃyutta Nikāya* 30.7–16 (SN 30.7, PTS SN iii 248).
1. The Supaṇṇa Chapter.
The Ten Discourses on the Benefit of Giving Eggs.
Setting at Sāvatthī.
Sitting to one side, that bhikkhu said this to the Blessed One:
“What, venerable sir, is the cause, what is the reason, why someone here, with the breakup of the body, after death, is reborn in the company of egg-born *supaṇṇas*?
“Here, bhikkhu, someone acts in two ways by body, acts in two ways by speech, and acts in two ways by mind.”
He has heard:
“The egg-born supaṇṇas are long-lived, beautiful, and abound in happiness.
It occurs to him:
‘Oh, that after the breakup of the body, after death, I might be reborn in the company of the egg-born supaṇṇas!
He gives food … [and so on] … he gives drink.
He gives clothing … he gives a vehicle … he gives a garland …
He gives perfume… he gives ointment… he gives a bed…
He gives a dwelling place...
he gives lighting.
With the breakup of the body, after death, he is reborn into the company of the egg-born supaṇṇas.
“Monk, this is the cause, this is the condition, by which someone here, with the breakup of the body, after death, is reborn in the company of egg-born *supaṇṇas*.
(The sixteenth.
*Saṃyutta Nikāya* 30.17–46 (SN 30.17, PTS SN iii 248)
1. The Supaṇṇa Chapter:
The Discourse on the Benefit of Giving Water-born [Lotuses].
Setting at Sāvatthī.
Seated to one side, that bhikkhu said this to the Blessed One:
"What, venerable sir, is the cause, what is the reason, why here some person, with the breakup of the body, after death, [is reborn] among the egg-born supaṇṇas...
[or] among the moisture-born supaṇṇas..."
“...is he reborn in the company of spontaneously born supaṇṇas?
“Here, bhikkhu, a certain person acts with duplicity by body, acts with duplicity by speech, and acts with duplicity by mind.
He has heard:”
‘The spontaneously born supaṇṇas have long lives, are beautiful, and abound in happiness.
It occurs to him:
‘Oh, that after the breakup of the body, after death, I might be reborn in the company of the spontaneously born supaṇṇas!’
Thus he gives food...
[and so on] ...he gives drink... [and so on] ...he gives lighting.
Thus, with the breakup of the body after death, he is reborn into the company of spontaneously born *supaṇṇas*.
This, monk, is the cause, this is the condition, by which someone here, with the breakup of the body after death, is reborn into the company of spontaneously born *supaṇṇas*.
Thus ends the forty-sixth discourse.
(Thus, by way of summary, there are forty-six discourses.
The first chapter, the Supaṇṇa Vagga.
Its summary verse:
They take away the pure [state],
and the one who acts in two ways takes four;
the gifts and benefits number forty.
"Supaṇṇas, well-expounded.
The Saṃyutta Nikāya on Supaṇṇas is complete.
